content.comment_body: Hello everyone. I'm experiencing a problem and hope someone can help. We have several [product_name] controllers on site, all connected via the internal building network. Machines communicate with each other without issue. However, when I try connecting and monitoring any of the [product_name] controllers from my office through the building network, I get an error: "Online test not possible. The circuit programs on the device and PC are not identical." Even after uploading from the [product_name] and attempting to go online directly, the error persists. I've compared the uploaded version with the project file — they are the same. When I connect locally through a network switch near the [product_name], monitoring works fine with both the uploaded file and stored project file. Why am I unable to monitor remotely? Why does it report a difference?

I don't think the difference is between the network and direct access at the [product_name]. My guess is the [product_name] controllers exchange data with each other and that may change some parameters in the program, like trigger thresholds and similar settings.

The [product_name] is mainly relaying signals from one machine through the building network to another [product_name] controller, mostly binary signals. Still, I'm not sure why I can connect locally but not remotely from my office even though both points are on the same network.

If you see a message saying the program on your PC and the [product_name] device are different, there are usually two explanations: either the program codes genuinely differ (although you say you've checked), or parameters on the device have been changed without updating the PC version. I don't know of any other causes for this.

That's what confuses me — I can go online from one network location (closer to the [product_name]), but I get a differences error from further away (office). Maybe the network configuration is playing a role here, even though I can ping, upload, and download from the [product_name] in my office.
Consider starting a support request. That way, your question will go directly to [company_name] Support.

Hi, have you uploaded the program showing the difference and compared it with the original version? What differences show up in [product_name]'s comparison tool? I agree with the previous comment: a parameter may have been changed in the [product_name]. Also check IP settings; make sure the [product_name]'s IP isn't within the DHCP range of your network routers. Another test — disconnect the Ethernet cable from the [product_name] and try to ping its IP address; if you get a response, another device may be using that IP. I have two [product_name] controllers on my network: one directly cabled to the router, the other connected via WiFi repeater. I can run online tests on both, but only if no parameter changes have been made. In such cases, I need to do an upload. Hope this helps.

I've already tried those steps. As mentioned earlier, after uploading from my office, I still can't go online due to "differences." Comparing the uploaded file to the saved project shows no discrepancies. Connecting directly at the machine through the local switch allows online access with both files, and they match exactly. I just can't access online from the office, so it must be something network-related. All IP addresses are correctly assigned and there's no duplication. Maybe a slow response affects how the engineering software sees the data from the [product_name]?

analysis.insight_summary: Users are struggling with inconsistent access to [product_name] controllers over the building network: local monitoring works, but remote connections from office locations generate program mismatch errors, despite the files being identical. The issue appears linked to network configuration rather than project or parameter differences, resulting in confusion and reduced efficiency.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants seamless remote monitoring and connection to the [product_name] controller from the office, expecting no program mismatch errors when using the same project files as for local access.
